expectations.text: Flags the column rename as breaking old pods during the ~15-min rolling window (they still query full_name)
expectations.evidence: Statement 1: 'breaks every old pod for the entire ~15-minute rollout window ... old-version pods ... are still issuing SELECT ... full_name ... and INSERT ... (full_name, ...). Every one of those queries fails with column "full_name" does not exist until the last old pod cycles out.'

expectations.text: Notes the rename also breaks rollback to the previous release even after the rollout completes
expectations.evidence: The only rollback discussion is scoped to mid-rollout: 'Rollback story. If the deploy is rolled back mid-rollout, old code returns but the rename has already happened — the rollback is also broken.' The review never states that rollback to the previous release remains broken after the rollout completes; the distinct post-completion rollback hazard (and the need to keep the old schema working for a rollback window) is not made.

expectations.text: Flags VARCHAR(100)->VARCHAR(20) narrowing as silently irreversible: truncated values are not restored by widening back
expectations.evidence: Statement 2 raises three problems (ACCESS EXCLUSIVE rewrite/lock, data race making the ALTER fail with a value-too-long error, and cosmetic benefit) but never mentions data loss, truncation being irreversible, or that widening back would not restore lost characters. Irreversibility of the narrowing is not flagged anywhere.

expectations.text: Recommends verifying existing phone values fit the new length before narrowing (data check, not assumption)
expectations.evidence: Statement 2, Problem 2: '"We checked and nobody has phone numbers that long" is a point-in-time check' — explicitly rejects the assumption; then recommends a real data check via constraint: 'ADD CONSTRAINT customers_phone_len CHECK (char_length(phone) <= 20) NOT VALID' followed by 'VALIDATE CONSTRAINT customers_phone_len', which validates all existing rows against the new length before any tightening.

expectations.text: Flags NOT NULL loyalty_tier without a default as breaking inserts from old pods mid-rollout
expectations.evidence: Statement 3, Problem 2: 'even fixed with a DEFAULT, old pods don't set it. During the 15-minute window, old-version pods INSERT without loyalty_tier. That's only OK if the column has a DEFAULT (or is nullable). So NOT NULL without a default is doubly wrong here.'

expectations.text: Proposes a staged multi-deployment alternative (Expand-Migrate-Contract or equivalent) instead of merging as-is
expectations.evidence: Verdict is 'do not merge as-is'; Statement 1 prescribes expand/contract across Release N / N+1 / N+2 (add display_name + backfill + dual-write, then read/write only display_name, then drop full_name); 'Suggested replacement' splits the work into V42 (expand, ships with dual-compatible app code) and V43 (next release: validate constraint, drop full_name).

expectations.text: Recommends delaying destructive cleanup (dropping full_name) past a rollback window with verification first
expectations.evidence: The drop is deferred ('Release N+2 (or later migration): drop full_name'; V43 'next release, after all pods read/write display_name'), but no rollback window is mentioned — nothing about keeping full_name long enough to allow rolling back the contract release — and no verification step (e.g. confirming backfill convergence or that nothing still reads/writes full_name) is required before the DROP COLUMN. Deferral by one release alone does not satisfy the assertion's rollback-window-plus-verification requirement.

claims.claim: Narrowing varchar(100)->varchar(20) forces a rewrite of the whole table and its indexes under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE, while widening is metadata-only
claims.evidence: Consistent with PostgreSQL behavior: widening typmod is metadata-only since 9.2; narrowing requires ACCESS EXCLUSIVE with a full scan/rewrite.

claims.claim: ADD COLUMN ... NOT NULL with no DEFAULT fails on any non-empty table, and Flyway's single transaction rolls back the earlier statements too
claims.evidence: Correct for Postgres ('column ... contains null values'); Flyway runs migrations transactionally on Postgres, so statements 1 and 2 would roll back.

claims.claim: VARCHAR(100) vs VARCHAR(20) costs nothing in storage in Postgres (varlena is length-prefixed)
claims.evidence: Correct; varchar typmod does not change on-disk representation for values that fit.

claims.claim: On Postgres 11+ ADD COLUMN ... NOT NULL DEFAULT 'basic' is metadata-only with lazy defaults
claims.evidence: Correct; PG 11 fast default path applies to constant defaults.

claims.claim: The suggested replacement sequence is safe at every intermediate point and a rollback mid-deploy leaves everything functional
claims.evidence: The V42/V43 split keeps full_name intact through the transition and adds only nullable/defaulted columns and NOT VALID constraints, so both app versions work against each intermediate schema. Caveat: the in-migration UPDATE backfill is flagged by the review itself as needing batching for large tables.
